concerns.text: FR-011 and SC-003 require the system to calculate and report the global semantic validity pass-rate for each σ level. T029 describes the sweep loop and recording the collapse point, but does not explicitly mandate the calculation and storage of the pass-rate metric itself (e.g., to a CSV or JSON) which is required for the final analysis and reporting. T031 only logs progress, not the metric.

FR-006 and FR-009 require filtering pairs based on BOTH input drift (FR-009) and output validity (FR-006). T035 explicitly mentions consuming `validity_log.csv` (input drift) but fails to mandate consuming the output validity results (from FR-006 checks) to exclude pairs that failed the BERTScore/perplexity check. This risks including invalid outputs in the statistical analysis.

FR-012 requires the system to automatically switch to Wilcoxon if n < 30 AND report the reduced statistical power. T049 mentions switching the test and logging a warning, but does not explicitly mandate the calculation and reporting of the 'reduced statistical power' metric in the output, leaving SC-005 partially unmet.

SC-006 requires measuring the distribution of the 'validity collapse point' across all task types. T037 describes calculating the statistical distribution (mean, std, histogram) but does not explicitly mandate storing the raw list of collapse points per task type in the output JSON, which is necessary for future re-analysis or verification of the distribution calculation.

FR-003 requires recording the 'validity collapse point' and excluding that σ and all higher values from analysis DURING the sweep. T010b refactors the loop into `run_sweep` but does not explicitly mandate that this function must implement the early-exit logic and recording of the collapse point, risking that the sweep continues past the collapse point.
